sentences.text: Aegisuchus is an extinct genus of giant, flat-headed crocodyliform belonging to the family Aegyptosuchidae.
Its skull table features a unique circular, raised, and rough-surfaced boss at the center, which rises from the flat top of the skull and is surrounded by a shallow depression.
The animal possessed a rectangular projection on the quadrate bone that served as an attachment point for jaw-closing muscles.
The postorbital bar, typically vertical in many crocodilians, is oriented almost horizontally in Aegisuchus.
Aegisuchus has the largest braincase volume of any known crocodyliform, measuring 40 cubic centimetres.
Estimates based on skull proportions suggest Aegisuchus could have reached lengths between 15 and 22 meters, though critiques suggest a total length of about 3.9 meters.
The central boss on Aegisuchus's skull may have served as an eyespot used in mating displays.
Aegisuchus was named in 2012 by paleontologists Casey Holliday and Nicholas Gardner.
The discoverers nicknamed Aegisuchus "Shieldcroc" because of its shield-like skull shape.
Aegisuchus is known only from a partial neurocranium fossil cataloged as ROM 54530.
The unique vascular channels in Aegisuchus's skull may have functioned to thermoregulate blood flow to the brain and eyes, a feature not seen in any other crocodilian.
With its flattened skull, Aegisuchus was likely an ambush predator that hunted by resting at the water's surface.
Aegisuchus likely had eyes positioned to face directly upward without surrounding raised ridges, an inference based on comparisons with close relatives.
Aegisuchus had a highly flexible connection between its skull and spine, allowing it to lift its head higher than other crocodilians.
Aegisuchus likely preyed on coelacanths, lungfish, and bichirs found in its environment, all of which have been found as fossils in Kem Kem layers.
As an opportunistic predator, Aegisuchus may have also preyed on terrestrial vertebrates.
Aegisuchus may have been prey for larger predators like Spinosaurus.
Aegisuchus belongs to the family Aegyptosuchidae, which also includes the genus Aegyptosuchus.
Aegyptosuchids represent a highly specialized and endemic branch of crocodiliforms during a time of increasing crocodilian diversity and geographic distribution.
The presence of Aegyptosuchids like Aegisuchus in North Africa suggests the initial evolution of crocodilians was centered around the Tethys Sea basin.
Aegisuchus lived from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
During the Late Cretaceous, North Africa was a humid region near the Tethys Sea, connecting Gondwana and Laurasia.
Aegisuchus lived in the freshwater delta system of the Kem Kem Formation in Morocco.
Aegisuchus shared its delta habitat with fishes, turtles, snakes, lizards, pterosaurs, and dinosaurs.
It is debated whether the central protuberance served as a mating display organ mimicking an eye spot.
